description: Parser config contains an entity descriptor for MapGroup that reads the newgroup / endgroup blocks in constants/map_constants.asm
steps: Open the project parser config
Verify that a MapGroup entity descriptor exists targeting constants/map_constants.asm
Verify the descriptor uses a table type with the newgroup macro as the header pattern and endgroup as the footer pattern
Run the parser against the reference pokecrystal codebase
Verify that the intermediate JSON contains a MapGroup array with one entry per group (OLIVINE, MAHOGANY, DUNGEONS … 26 total in vanilla pokecrystal)
Verify each MapGroup entry carries group_name (e.g. OLIVINE) and group_id (numeric index from const_value)

description: Parser config contains an entity descriptor for GameMap (dimensions) that reads map_const rows from constants/map_constants.asm
steps: Verify that a GameMap entity descriptor exists targeting constants/map_constants.asm
Verify the descriptor uses a row pattern matching the map_const macro, capturing map_name, width, and height
Run the parser against the reference codebase
Verify the intermediate JSON GameMap entries include map_name (e.g. OLIVINE_GYM), width, and height
Verify the group association is captured so each map is linked to its enclosing newgroup block

description: Parser config contains an entity descriptor for GameMap (data properties) that reads map macro calls from data/maps/maps.asm
steps: Verify that a GameMap entity descriptor exists targeting data/maps/maps.asm
Verify the descriptor uses the map macro pattern capturing: display_name (PascalCase), tileset, environment, landmark, music, phone_service, palette, fish_group
Run the parser
Verify the intermediate JSON merges the maps.asm-sourced properties onto the correct GameMap entities (matched by map name constant, normalised to UPPER_SNAKE_CASE)
Spot-check: OLIVINE_GYM should have tileset=TILESET_CHAMPIONS_ROOM, environment=INDOOR, music=MUSIC_GYM, palette=PALETTE_DAY

description: Parser config contains an entity descriptor for MapGroupRoofAssignment that reads the MapGroupRoofs table in data/maps/roofs.asm
steps: Verify that a MapGroupRoofAssignment entity descriptor exists targeting data/maps/roofs.asm
Verify the descriptor reads per-group roof index values from the db rows in the MapGroupRoofs table
Run the parser
Verify each MapGroup's roof assignment is captured correctly (e.g. group 1 Olivine → ROOF_OLIVINE, group 3 Dungeons → -1 meaning no roof)

description: Parser config contains an entity descriptor for OutdoorSpriteGroup that reads per-group sprite ID lists from data/maps/outdoor_sprites.asm
steps: Verify that an OutdoorSpriteGroup entity descriptor exists targeting data/maps/outdoor_sprites.asm
Verify the descriptor captures the group label (e.g. PalletGroupSprites) and the list of SPRITE_* constant values that follow it
Run the parser
Verify that each MapGroup entry in the intermediate JSON has an associated list of valid outdoor sprite IDs

description: Parser config contains entity descriptors for SpriteConstant, TilesetConstant, MusicConstant, and LandmarkConstant pulled from their respective constants files
steps: Verify a SpriteConstant descriptor targets constants/sprite_constants.asm and captures SPRITE_* names and their ordinal values
Verify a TilesetConstant descriptor targets constants/tileset_constants.asm and captures TILESET_* names
Verify a MusicConstant descriptor targets constants/music_constants.asm and captures MUSIC_* names
Verify a LandmarkConstant descriptor targets constants/landmark_constants.asm and captures LANDMARK_* names
Run the parser and confirm intermediate JSON contains fully populated arrays for each constant type

description: Parser config contains entity descriptors for environment, palette, and fish-group constants from constants/map_data_constants.asm
steps: Verify an EnvironmentConstant descriptor captures TOWN, ROUTE, INDOOR, CAVE, GATE, DUNGEON values
Verify a PaletteConstant descriptor captures PALETTE_AUTO, PALETTE_DAY, PALETTE_NITE, PALETTE_MORN, PALETTE_DARK
Verify a FishGroupConstant descriptor captures FISHGROUP_NONE through FISHGROUP_QWILFISH_NO_SWARM
Run the parser and confirm correct entries in the intermediate JSON

description: Parser config contains an entity descriptor for MapAttributes that reads the map_attributes macro from data/maps/attributes.asm
steps: Verify a MapAttributes descriptor targets data/maps/attributes.asm
Verify the descriptor captures: map name, border_block value, and connection flags (north / south / east / west)
Run the parser
Spot-check an entry: a map with a south connection should show that connection flag as set in the intermediate JSON

description: HLR factory creates typed MapGroup objects from the intermediate JSON with all expected fields populated
steps: Run the parser to produce intermediate JSON from the reference codebase
Pass the intermediate JSON to the HLR factory
Verify the resulting MapGroup objects have: groupId (numeric), groupName (string, e.g. OLIVINE), roofType (ROOF_* constant or null for groups with value -1), outdoorSpriteIds (string array)
Verify there are 26 MapGroup objects in canonical pokecrystal

description: HLR factory creates typed GameMap objects from the intermediate JSON with all expected fields populated and correctly linked to their parent MapGroup
steps: Pass intermediate JSON to the HLR factory

Verify each GameMap object has: mapConstant (e.g. OLIVINE_GYM), groupId, mapIndex (position within the group), tileset, environment, landmark, music, phoneServiceEnabled (boolean), palette, fishGroup, width, height
Verify each GameMap.groupId matches the groupId of exactly one MapGroup object
Spot-check: OLIVINE_GYM map should be in the OLIVINE group (groupId 1) at index 2

description: HLR factory correctly merges multi-file data: GameMap fields sourced from map_constants.asm and maps.asm are combined into one HLR object
steps: Verify that for each GameMap, properties parsed from constants/map_constants.asm (width, height) and properties parsed from data/maps/maps.asm (tileset, environment, landmark, music, etc.) appear on the same GameMap HLR object
Verify that the entity_id used for the merge key is the map constant name (e.g. OLIVINE_GYM, normalised to UPPER_SNAKE_CASE)
Confirm that no duplicate GameMap objects exist for the same map constant after merging

description: IPC channel GET_MAP_HLR_SNAPSHOT returns a fully serializable DTO containing all MapGroup and GameMap data
steps: Register the channel in registerMapIpc.ts and confirm it is wired in registerIpc.ts
Invoke GET_MAP_HLR_SNAPSHOT from the renderer side
Verify the returned DTO contains a mapGroups array and a gameMaps array (or gameMaps nested inside each group)
Verify the DTO contains no class instances or non-serializable values
Verify the DTO is correctly typed in src/shared/types/

description: Parser metadata JSON for each map-related file contains one entry per extracted property, enabling the patcher to locate and update each value
steps: Parse the reference codebase
Inspect the parser metadata JSON for data/maps/maps.asm

Verify that each captured map macro property (tileset, environment, landmark, music, phone_service, palette, fish_group) has its own metadata entry with entity_id, property name, value, pattern, rawLine, and line_num
Verify the same structure exists for constants/map_constants.asm entries (width, height per map_const row)

description: A Map Groups Explorer panel is accessible from the Activity Bar and lists all parsed map groups
steps: Open Crystal Studio with a parsed workspace
Click the Maps icon in the Activity Bar
Verify that the Map Groups Explorer panel opens in the sidebar
Verify that all 26 map groups from the parsed codebase are shown as rows in the panel
Verify each group row displays the group name (e.g. Olivine, Mahogany)

description: Each map group row shows a badge with the number of maps it contains
steps: Open the Map Groups Explorer panel
Locate the Olivine group row
Verify a badge shows the count 14 (OLIVINE has 14 maps in vanilla pokecrystal)
Verify that collapsing the group hides the badge or keeps it visible but the map list is hidden (consistent with VS Code explorer conventions)

description: Each map group row is collapsible and expandable, revealing the list of maps it contains
steps: Open the Map Groups Explorer panel
Click the expand toggle on the Olivine group row
Verify that the list of maps within Olivine is shown beneath the group row
Verify that map entries show their display name (e.g. Olivine Pokecenter 1F)
Click the collapse toggle and verify the map list is hidden

description: The game start map is visually highlighted with a distinct indicator in the Map Groups Explorer
steps: Open Crystal Studio with a parsed pokecrystal workspace
Open the Map Groups Explorer panel
Expand the map group that contains the map designated as the game start map (controlled by the startMap project config field)
Verify that the start map row carries a distinct visual indicator (e.g. a home icon or accent colour) not shown on other maps
Verify that only one map visible in the explorer carries the start indicator at any given time

description: The start map designation is read from a configurable field in the project config and defaults to NEW_BARK_TOWN for new pokecrystal projects
steps: Inspect the project config Zod schema and verify a startMap string field exists (defaulting to NEW_BARK_TOWN)
Open Crystal Studio with a new pokecrystal workspace
Verify that NEW_BARK_TOWN is highlighted as the start map in the Map Groups Explorer
Change startMap to PLAYERS_HOUSE_2F in the project config
Reload the session and verify PLAYERS_HOUSE_2F is now highlighted instead

description: Selecting a map group in the explorer populates the Properties Panel with group-level details
steps: Open the Map Groups Explorer panel and expand any group
Click the group header row (not a child map)
Verify the Properties Panel shows: group name, roof type (or None if -1), outdoor sprite count
Verify the Properties Panel updates when a different group is selected

description: Selecting a map in the explorer populates the Properties Panel with map-level details
steps: Open the Map Groups Explorer panel, expand a group, and click a map row

Verify the Properties Panel shows: map constant name, display name, tileset, environment type, landmark / location, music track, time-of-day palette, fishing group, and map dimensions (width × height in blocks)
Verify the Properties Panel updates correctly when a different map is selected
Verify selecting a map in a different group also works correctly after switching groups
